miniProject.title: Disaggregated serving with owned handoffs and evidence labels
miniProject.brief: Extend `sim/` with sharded, disaggregated and topology-aware serving plans and prove their handoffs preserve identity under faults. The evidence-labeled comparison ranks colocated against phase-separated serving and feeds gateway and capacity work.
steps: Extend `sim/` with replica and tensor-parallel shard plans plus a per-rank ownership ledger, and check sharded forwards against an unsharded reference with own tests. Keep the ledger with replicated-head and over-budget rejection cases.

Reproduce the Day 17 pipeline bubble timeline on CPU and extend it with expert skew and position-shard accounting, checking boundaries against the notebook experiment. Keep timelines and a case where skew outweighs byte counts.

Build a per-layer communication ledger with a shared-link contention model, then sweep small-batch latency against memory capacity to surface a feasible plan that loses after startup. Keep the ledger and the losing plan.

Implement deterministic cache-aware routing in `sim/` with stated tie-breaks and compare it against load-only and predicted-waiting policies under skew and stale information, passing the TensorTonic routing problem. Keep traces and a hot-prefix loss.

Add separate phase queues with a fixed-budget pool sweep and first-token against KV-ready traces, plus serialized and overlapped handoff timelines with bounded credits, slow-receiver backpressure, tier-restore comparison, heterogeneous service and reserve-aware resize. Keep traces and the break-even decision.

Implement a versioned KV envelope with a mapping oracle and checksum plus incompatible-identity rejection, then replay cancellation, rank, transfer and duplicate faults with fencing and bounded retirement through a saturation-tested equal-budget comparison with ablations against hand ledgers. Keep fault traces and a negative regime.
deliverables: Shard, ownership and communication ledgers with differential checks and the losing latency plan.
Routing, phase-pool and handoff evidence in `sim/` with traces, break-even decision and fault cases.
Evidence-labeled comparison in `reports/` with equal-budget goodput, utilization, traffic and cost plus tests.

checks.name: TensorTonic cache-aware routing
checks.note: Free public cases for locality, tie-breaks and rejection; add own load tests.

checks.name: 100 Days Day 17 pipeline bubble
checks.note: Run the bubble break-even item and check boundaries with own timeline enumeration.

rubric.pass: Ownership and communication ledgers reconcile, sharded forwards match the unsharded reference, and the losing latency plan is kept.
rubric.strong: A second sharding or topology case is checked, and startup versus bandwidth terms are separated.

rubric.pass: The router passes public cases plus own tie tests, and phase-pool traces show queueing, transfer and reserve costs.
rubric.strong: A hot-prefix counterexample explains the loss, and resize keeps only ready workers counted.

rubric.pass: Envelope, fencing and retirement tests pass, and the equal-budget comparison keeps saturation traces and a negative regime.
rubric.strong: Hand-ledger replay matches, and goodput, utilization, traffic and cost are labeled by evidence tier.

miniProject.feedsInto: `sim/` topology replay, handoff envelope and evidence labels feed `gateway/` isolation and the capstone comparison.
